- Split CI Python linting into two parallel jobs to cut `python-lint` wall time. Root cause: pylint runs single-process (`-j1`) on Linux CI (~100s of the ~166s job); ruff is ~0.1s and pyright is ~36s.
  - **`python-lint`**: ruff + pylint, with pylint forced to all cores.
  - **`python-pyright`** (new): pyright only.
- Restructure the Makefile so CI runs the halves separately while local `make py-lint` stays the unchanged superset:
  - `py-lint: py-lint-main py-typecheck` (umbrella; local-dev entry, same output and order).
  - `py-lint-main`: ruff + pylint.
  - `py-typecheck`: pyright.
  - Keep the `PYLINT_JOBS ?= $(shell ...)` sysconf auto-detect unchanged (local fallback).
- Force pylint to all cores on CI only via job-level `env: PYLINT_JOBS: "0"` on `python-lint`; `make`'s `?=` keeps the env value, so local behavior is untouched.
- Move `actions/setup-node` from `python-lint` (no longer runs pyright) to `python-pyright`.
- Register `python-pyright` as a first-class fixable job (drift guard + `/implement --merge` replay) using `make` targets, so replay honors the Makefile `PYLINT_JOBS` fallback locally while CI overrides via env.
- Keep `python-lint-duplicate-code` untouched (separate in-flight design issue; must stay `-j1`).
- Update `docs/linting.md` prose describing the `python-lint` job.

Keep the existing note that local `make lint` does not run `py-lint`.

### Edge cases

- Branch protection may still require only the old `python-lint` status. Add `python-pyright` as a required check in GitHub settings (outside this repo), or pyright stops gating merges.
- Keep all lint commands rooted in `python/` so `.pylintrc` and `pyrightconfig.json` resolve.
- `make py-lint` remains the local superset (ruff + pylint + pyright); only CI jobs and replay use the narrower sub-targets.
- Do not split ruff into its own job; it runs ~0.1s.
- Do not touch `python-lint-duplicate-code` (separate in-flight design issue; must stay `-j1`).

### Failure modes

- YAML indentation errors can break the workflow; run `actionlint` locally.
- If a CI runner cannot do pylint multiprocessing, forcing `PYLINT_JOBS=0` could make `python-lint` fail rather than speed up. Standard `ubuntu-latest` supports it; the `env` override is trivially revertable, and the Makefile sysconf fallback still protects local/restricted hosts.
- If `python-pyright` is omitted from any mapping surface (`config.py` / `ci-failed-jobs.sh` / `test-ci-failed-jobs.sh`), `make test-ci-failed-jobs` fails and/or `/implement --merge` mis-classifies pyright failures.

### Testing strategy

- Run `make lint`, `make py-lint`, and `make py-test`.
- Run the full `python3 -m pytest python/test_ci_monitor.py` module to catch stale `("make", "py-lint")` stubs and missing `python-pyright` replay entries.
- Run `make test-ci-failed-jobs` (or its harness shard) to confirm the drift guard passes with `python-pyright`.
- If available, run `actionlint .github/workflows/ci.yaml`.
- Validate on CI:
  - `python-lint` no longer runs pyright and completes in roughly half or less of the prior ~166s.
  - `python-pyright` runs and fails independently on type errors.
  - Combined coverage still includes ruff, full pylint, duplicate-code pylint, pyright, and tests.

# CI splits `lint` into `lint-only` (pre-commit) and `test-harnesses`
# (regression harnesses). `lint` remains the local-dev convenience target
# that runs both, defined in terms of the two split targets to prevent drift.

py-lint:
	@$(PYTHON) -c 'import sys; raise SystemExit(0 if sys.version_info >= (3, 11) else 1)' \
		|| (printf '%s\n' "ERROR: make py-lint requires Python 3.11 or newer (PYTHON=$(PYTHON))" >&2; exit 1)
	# pylint runs with all cores when the host supports the required process-pool
	# semaphore query. Some restricted local sandboxes deny that query, so they
	# fall back to a single worker. duplicate-code is disabled here (.pylintrc)
	# and runs single-process in py-lint-duplicate-code.
	cd python && ruff check . && pylint -j $(PYLINT_JOBS) . && pyright

py-lint-duplicate-code:
	@$(PYTHON) -c 'import sys; raise SystemExit(0 if sys.version_info >= (3, 11) else 1)' \
		|| (printf '%s\n' "ERROR: make py-lint-duplicate-code requires Python 3.11 or newer (PYTHON=$(PYTHON))" >&2; exit 1)
	# Duplicate-code (R0801) runs as a dedicated single-process pass: pylint's
	# similarities checker is incorrect under -j>1 (each worker sees only a slice
	# of files), so it must run with -j 1. Kept out of `py-lint` (which disables
	# duplicate-code via .pylintrc) so the main lint pass parallelizes; this is
	# the CI `python-lint-duplicate-code` job. See issue #4480.
	cd python && pylint --disable=all --enable=duplicate-code -j 1 .

py-test:
	@$(PYTHON) -c 'import sys; raise SystemExit(0 if sys.version_info >= (3, 11) else 1)' \
		|| (printf '%s\n' "ERROR: make py-test requires Python 3.11 or newer (PYTHON=$(PYTHON))" >&2; exit 1)
	# --durations=0 emits per-test timing so CI shards (PYTEST_SHARD_ID /
	# PYTEST_SHARD_COUNT, see python/conftest.py) can be rebalanced by wall time.
	cd python && $(PYTHON) -m pytest --durations=0

name: CI

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - main
  # Run the full workflow on push to main so the pre-commit hook-env
  # cache populates under the default-branch scope. PRs from feature
  # branches can read default-branch caches but cannot read each
  # other's, so without this trigger every fresh PR pays the
  # ~1m 40s cold-install cost on the lint job. The cost of running
  # all jobs on each merge to main is accepted as a side effect.
  # Issue #1034.
  push:
    branches:
      - main

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  # Force all JavaScript-based actions (including transitive sub-actions like
  # the actions/cache@v4 carried inside actions/setup-node and
  # actions/setup-python) to run under Node.js 24.  Suppresses the deprecation
  # warning that fires on every job:
  #   "Node.js 20 actions are deprecated."
  # Per GitHub release notes 2025-09-19, Node 20 is removed from runners on
  # 2026-09-16; this env var becomes the default on 2026-06-02.
  FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24: "true"

jobs:
  # External-tool linters only: markdownlint, jsonlint, and actionlint.
  # All local bash/python linters run in the parallel `lint-local` job.
  # `agent-lint`, `agnix`, and `shellcheck` run in their dedicated jobs.
  # `gitleaks` working-tree scan moved to the `gitleaks` job to shed ~40s
  # from this job's critical path. Test harnesses run in the separate
  # `test-harnesses` job. Mermaid fence lint and SIGPIPE safety lint run in
  # the parallel `lint-mermaid` job (closes #2080).
  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"
          cache: pip
          cache-dependency-path: .github/workflows/requirements-lint.txt
      - uses: actions/cache@v5
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/pre-commit
          key: pre-commit-${{ hashFiles('.pre-commit-config.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: |
            pre-commit-
      - name: Install lint dependencies
        env:
          PIP_RETRIES: "5"
          PIP_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT: "30"
        run: pip install -r .github/workflows/requirements-lint.txt
      - name: Run pre-commit linters (external tools)
        # Runs markdownlint, jsonlint, and actionlint only.
        # `agent-lint`, `agnix`, and `shellcheck` run in dedicated jobs.
        # `gitleaks` moved to the `gitleaks` job. Local bash/python linters
        # run in `lint-local`. If a dedicated job is removed, drop its hook
        # name from SKIP to restore CI coverage. Issue #1034.
        env:
          SKIP: agnix,lint-mermaid-fences,shellcheck,gitleaks,agent-lint,lint-skill-invocations,lint-literal-counts,lint-no-raw-stderr-after-quiet-init,lint-gh-body-inline,lint-bash32,bash-syntax-check,check-topology-rule-paths,lint-readability-preamble,lint-renderer-substitution-safety,lint-skill-md-flag-signature,lint-bare-grep-probe,lint-codex-exec-auth,lint-awk-multibyte-regex
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          log="$(mktemp)"
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            set +e
            make lint-only 2>&1 | tee "$log"
            rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
            set -e

            if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
              exit 0
            fi
            if ! grep -Fq 'failed to download https://github.com/zhupanov/agent-lint/releases/download/' "$log"; then
              exit "$rc"
            fi
            if [ "$attempt" -eq 3 ]; then
              exit "$rc"
            fi

            echo "agent-lint release download failed; retrying make lint-only" >&2
            sleep 10
          done

  # Local bash/python linters — split from `lint` into a parallel job so
  # both halves run concurrently. Runs lint-skill-invocations,
  # lint-literal-counts, lint-bash32, lint-renderer-substitution-safety,
  # lint-awk-multibyte-regex, and all other local hooks while `lint` runs
  # the external-tool hooks (markdownlint, jsonlint, agent-lint, actionlint).
  lint-local:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"
          cache: pip
          cache-dependency-path: .github/workflows/requirements-lint.txt
      - uses: actions/cache@v5
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/pre-commit
          key: pre-commit-${{ hashFiles('.pre-commit-config.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: |
            pre-commit-
      - name: Install lint dependencies
        env:
          PIP_RETRIES: "5"
          PIP_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT: "30"
        run: pip install -r .github/workflows/requirements-lint.txt
      - name: Run pre-commit linters (local)
        # Runs only local bash/python linters. External tools (markdownlint,
        # jsonlint, actionlint) run in `lint`. Dedicated-job hooks
        # (gitleaks, agnix, shellcheck, agent-lint) are skipped here.
        env:
          SKIP: agnix,lint-mermaid-fences,shellcheck,gitleaks,markdownlint,jsonlint,agent-lint,actionlint
        run: make lint-only

  # Mermaid fence lint and SIGPIPE safety lint — split from the `lint` job
  # into a parallel job so both halves run concurrently (closes #2080).
  # Requires fetch-depth: 0 so `python3 python/cli.py lint mermaid-fences --changed-only` can
  # resolve `origin/<base>...HEAD` even on PRs whose merge base is deeper
  # than the default depth=1 shallow window.
  lint-mermaid:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          # Fetch the full history so the Python Mermaid lint
          # (`python3 python/cli.py lint mermaid-fences --changed-only`) can resolve `origin/<base>...HEAD` even on
          # PRs whose merge base is deeper than the default depth=1
          # shallow window. The prior shallow checkout could yield an
          # empty / wrong diff while the lint step still exited 0,
          # silently disabling Mermaid CI coverage (closes #1426
          # follow-up D — round-2 review).
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 'lts/*'
          cache: npm
          # Track the lockfile so a lockfile-only bump invalidates the
          # npm cache (closes #1426 follow-up FINDING_1).
          cache-dependency-path: mermaid-lint/package-lock.json
      - uses: actions/cache@v5
        id: node-modules-cache
        with:
          path: mermaid-lint/node_modules
          # Key on both package.json and package-lock.json so a
          # dependency-manifest change that doesn't update the lockfile
          # still invalidates this cache (closes #1576).
          key: node-modules-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('mermaid-lint/package.json', 'mermaid-lint/package-lock.json') }}
      - uses: actions/cache@v5
        id: puppeteer-cache
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/puppeteer
          # Mirror the cache-dependency-path key on the lockfile so the
          # Chromium cache invalidates whenever resolved Puppeteer
          # changes — even via lockfile-only bumps (closes #1426
          # follow-up FINDING_1).
          key: puppeteer-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('mermaid-lint/package-lock.json') }}
      - name: Install Mermaid CLI
        # `npm ci` installs exactly from the committed lockfile and
        # fails if the lockfile is out of sync with package.json. This
        # is the conventional CI contract — `npm install` would tolerate
        # / silently update the lockfile, defeating the purpose of
        # committing it (closes #1426 follow-up FINDING_10).
        #
        # Mermaid CLI 11.x has no --parseOnly mode, so the Python lint
        # falls back to mmdc -i ... -o ....svg, which requires
        # Puppeteer's Chromium download. The puppeteer cache above
        # restores ~/.cache/puppeteer between runs so cold downloads
        # only happen when package-lock.json changes.
        #
        # Skipped only when BOTH node_modules and Puppeteer caches hit:
        # a node_modules hit with a puppeteer miss would leave Chromium
        # absent and break the mermaid lint step (closes #1576).
        if: steps.node-modules-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true' || steps.puppeteer-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        env:
          npm_config_fetch_retries: "5"
          npm_config_fetch_retry_factor: "2"
          npm_config_fetch_retry_mintimeout: "10000"
          npm_config_fetch_retry_maxtimeout: "120000"
        run: cd mermaid-lint && npm ci
      - name: Lint Mermaid fences (changed only)
        run: python3 python/cli.py lint mermaid-fences --changed-only
      - name: Pipe SIGPIPE safety lint
        run: bash scripts/test-pipe-sigpipe-safety.sh

  # Dedicated shellcheck jobs — split into `scripts` and `skills/.claude`
  # scopes running in parallel to halve wall-clock time. Each scope installs
  # the pinned shellcheck-py==0.11.0.1 binary directly (no pre-commit
  # overhead) and runs shellcheck -x in parallel via xargs. The pre-commit
  # `shellcheck` hook remains active for local `pre-commit run` and the dev
  # git-hook; CI skips it in `lint` and `lint-local` via the SKIP env var.
  # shellcheck-py pinned to 0.11.0.1 — keep in sync with .pre-commit-config.yaml on bump.
  shellcheck:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - scope: scripts
            paths: scripts
          - scope: skills
            paths: "skills .claude"
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"
          cache: pip
          # Key on .pre-commit-config.yaml since shellcheck-py is pinned there;
          # a pin bump invalidates the cache.
          cache-dependency-path: .pre-commit-config.yaml
      - name: Install shellcheck
        env:
          PIP_RETRIES: "5"
          PIP_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT: "30"
        run: pip install shellcheck-py==0.11.0.1
      - name: Run shellcheck (${{ matrix.scope }})
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          max_parallel="$(nproc 2>/dev/null || echo 1)"
          find ${{ matrix.paths }} -name "*.sh" -not -path "*/larch-logs/*" -print0 \
            | xargs -0 -r -n 1 -P "$max_parallel" shellcheck -x --exclude=SC2329 --

  # Regression harness shards (the `test-*` bash scripts in Makefile). Runs
  # as a parallel matrix in parallel with the `lint` and `shellcheck` jobs so

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ci-failed-jobs.sh — classify failed GitHub Actions jobs for local replay.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd -P)"
# shellcheck source=scripts/lib-quiet.sh
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib-quiet.sh"
larch_quiet_init

RUN_ID=""
REPO=""
OUTPUT_TSV=""

usage() {
    larch_err "Usage: ci-failed-jobs.sh --run-id RUN_ID --repo OWNER/REPO [--output-tsv PATH]"
}

die() {
    larch_err "ci-failed-jobs.sh: $1"
    usage
    exit 2
}

sanitize_list() {
    tr -cd '[:alnum:]_,=:-'
}

job_class() {
    case "$1" in
        lint|lint-local|lint-mermaid|shellcheck|test-harnesses|agent-lint|agent-sync|python-lint|python-lint-duplicate-code|python-tests|bash32-check)
            printf '%s\n' fixable
            ;;
        gitleaks|trufflehog)
            printf '%s\n' no-local-equivalent
            ;;
        *)
            printf '%s\n' no-local-equivalent
            ;;
    esac
}

reason_token() {
    case "$1" in
        malformed) printf '%s\n' malformed-job-name ;;
        gitleaks|trufflehog) printf '%s\n' history-scan ;;
        *) printf '%s\n' unknown-job-name ;;
    esac
}

while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in
        --run-id) [ "$#" -ge 2 ] || die "--run-id requires a value"; RUN_ID=$2; shift 2 ;;
        --repo) [ "$#" -ge 2 ] || die "--repo requires a value"; REPO=$2; shift 2 ;;
        --output-tsv) [ "$#" -ge 2 ] || die "--output-tsv requires a value"; OUTPUT_TSV=$2; shift 2 ;;
        --help) usage; exit 0 ;;
        *) die "unknown option: $1" ;;
    esac
done

[ -n "$RUN_ID" ] || die "--run-id is required"
[ -n "$REPO" ] || die "--repo is required"

tmp_stdout=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ci-failed-jobs.out.XXXXXX")
tmp_stderr=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ci-failed-jobs.err.XXXXXX")
cleanup() {
    rm -f "$tmp_stdout" "$tmp_stderr"
}
trap cleanup EXIT

gh_rc=0
gh run view "$RUN_ID" --repo "$REPO" --json jobs --jq '.jobs[] | select(.conclusion=="failure") | .name' \
    > "$tmp_stdout" 2> "$tmp_stderr" || gh_rc=$?

if [ "$gh_rc" -ne 0 ]; then
    if grep -Fq "is still in progress; logs will be available" "$tmp_stderr" "$tmp_stdout" 2>/dev/null; then
        exit 3
    fi
    while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
        larch_err "$(printf '%s' "$line" | sanitize_diagnostic_line)"
    done < "$tmp_stderr"
    exit 1
fi

if [ -n "$OUTPUT_TSV" ]; then
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUTPUT_TSV")"
    OUTPUT_TSV_TMP="${OUTPUT_TSV}.tmp.$$"
    : > "$OUTPUT_TSV_TMP"
else
    OUTPUT_TSV_TMP=""
fi

count=0
fixable_list=""
unfixable_list=""
matrix_re='^([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*)[[:space:]]+\(([0-9]+)\)$'
matrix_any_re='^([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*)[[:space:]]+\(([^)]*)\)$'
job_re='^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$'

while IFS= read -r raw_name || [ -n "$raw_name" ]; do
    raw_name=$(printf '%s' "$raw_name" | sanitize_diagnostic_line)
    [ -n "$raw_name" ] || continue
    # Aggregator gate jobs (e.g. test-harnesses-gate) mirror their matrix and
    # have no local fix; the underlying leg carries the real fix signal. Skip
    # them so they are neither counted nor classified as fixable/unfixable.
    case "$raw_name" in
        *-gate) continue ;;
    esac
    count=$((count + 1))

    job_name=$raw_name
    shard=""
    malformed=false

    if [[ "$raw_name" =~ $matrix_re ]]; then
        job_name=${BASH_REMATCH[1]}
        shard=${BASH_REMATCH[2]}
    elif [[ "$raw_name" =~ $matrix_any_re ]]; then
        job_name=${BASH_REMATCH[1]}
        shard=""
    fi

    if ! [[ "$job_name" =~ $job_re ]]; then
        malformed=true
        class=no-local-equivalent
        reason=$(reason_token malformed)
    else
        class=$(job_class "$job_name")
        reason=$(reason_token "$job_name")
    fi

    if [ -n "$OUTPUT_TSV_TMP" ]; then
        printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$job_name" "$shard" "$class" >> "$OUTPUT_TSV_TMP"
    else
        emit "$(printf '%s\t%s\t%s' "$job_name" "$shard" "$class")"
    fi

    token=$job_name
    [ -n "$shard" ] && token="${token}:${shard}"
    if [ "$class" = "fixable" ] && [ "$malformed" = false ]; then
        if [ -n "$fixable_list" ]; then fixable_list="${fixable_list},${token}"; else fixable_list=$token; fi
    else
        tuple="${token}=${reason}"
        if [ -n "$unfixable_list" ]; then unfixable_list="${unfixable_list},${tuple}"; else unfixable_list=$tuple; fi
    fi
done < "$tmp_stdout"

if [ -n "${OUTPUT_TSV_TMP:-}" ]; then
    mv "$OUTPUT_TSV_TMP" "$OUTPUT_TSV"
fi

emit_kv FAILED_JOBS_COUNT "$count"
emit_kv FAILED_JOBS_FIXABLE "$(printf '%s' "$fixable_list" | sanitize_list)"
emit_kv FAILED_JOBS_UNFIXABLE "$(printf '%s' "$unfixable_list" | sanitize_list)"
